atoms.a: Actually, Matt, I'm not sure we should go to Croatia. Planes produce a huge amount of pollution, and flying causes a lot of carbon emissions. What if we took the train to Paris instead? It's a much more eco-friendly way to travel.

instruction.text: Ordne den Personen ihre Positionen zu.

atoms.a: thinks flying is bad for the environment and wants to take the train to Paris instead
wants to take a cheap flight to Croatia and see the amazing beaches

atoms.sound: But flying is so much faster! Do you really think one short trip will make such a big difference? And anyway, isn't reducing emissions something governments are responsible for, rather than tourists like us?

Of course, governments have a huge responsibility. They need to make sustainable travel easier and reduce our dependence on fossil fuels. But if we don't think about our individual responsibility, too, we'll never be able to reduce our carbon footprint as a society.

instruction.text: Sind die Aussagen wahr oder falsch? Wähle aus.

atoms.a: Matt thinks that governments are responsible for reducing carbon emissions.
Leila says that individual actions are not important for reducing society's carbon footprint.

atoms.sound: Okay, I guess you're right. Taking the train sounds quite relaxing, to be honest. Is there anything else we should keep in mind for a more eco-friendly trip? I've heard that tourists waste a lot of resources.
It's true that tourism uses up a lot of resources, but if we use public transport and eat local, vegetarian meals, the environmental impact of our trip won't be so bad.
Alright, Leila. We're going to Paris. Let's start planning!
